etymology: From Astroturf, the artificial grass - a grassroots movement with the lawn manufactured.
trigger: A decision that needs to look like it has a constituency.
tell: A burst of new accounts using the same phrase, a "local" group with a Washington address, and a comment section that agrees too quickly.
counter: Ask who is paying, and when the group was incorporated. Grassroots has a membership list; astroturf has an invoice.

confused_with.tell: The rally is a crowd that showed up; astroturfing is a crowd that was ordered.

senses: The move of manufacturing the appearance of a movement: front groups, purchased lists, rented crowds, and comment sections that arrive on schedule.

It works because numbers are read as consent. A legislator cannot count the people behind the letters, so forty identical emails from forty constituents and forty from a vendor look the same in the inbox - and the vendor knows it.
example: *"Two hundred identical letters, three local groups sharing a PO box, and an **astroturfing** campaign that one staffer had drafted on a Tuesday."*
